coverage_notes: SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia 2014 Ohio State Buckeyes football team page - infobox plus its "Coaching staff" section (12 names). (2) Ohio State's own football roster/coaching-staff page archived on the Wayback Machine at 20141031180732 (Oct. 31, 2014, mid-season) - 15 names including all four graduate assistants. (3) Ohio State's "Coaching Staff / Support Staff" page archived at 20141010100906 (Oct. 10, 2014, mid-season) - adds the "Football Support Staff" block (Voltolini, Pantoni, Marotti, Parker, Schlegel, Uhlenhake). (4) The full Ohio State athletics staff directory archived at the same timestamp (redirects to a 20141008043321 snapshot) - this was the single richest source, giving the complete "Football" department table (24 rows) and the "Strength Training & Conditioning-Football" table (5 rows). (5) The 2014 Ohio State football media guide PDF (11.3 MB, 252 pp.) recovered from the Wayback Machine, page 2 of which carries the quick-facts staff box. (6) Individual archived Ohio State staff bio pages for Gillum, Jefferson, Parker and Uhlenhake. TOTAL: 32 people, all with at least one real citation. Breakdown: 1 head coach, 9 on-field assistants, 4 graduate assistants, 6 strength and conditioning (one unconfirmed - see below), 9 operations/personnel/administration, 2 football video, 1 medical. QUOTE-MATCHING CAVEAT - PLEASE READ. Every quote below was mechanically verified by me against a tag-stripped rendering of the live/archived page before submission. However, the two most valuable sources are HTML tables in which a person's NAME and their ROLE sit in two SEPARATE adjacent table cells with no whitespace between them in the source (`...>Greg GillumDir, High School Relations`). A combined "Name Role" quote would therefore NOT survive a naive tag-strip. For those rows I deliberately quoted only the role string - which is contiguous and verified present - and named the person in the accompanying `note`. Where a source did put name and role in one cell (the roster page, e.g. "Jon Carpenter - Graduate Assistant - Defense", and Wikipedia's bulleted list) I quoted the full combined string. Three quotes contain an HTML-encoded ampersand ("Assistant Strength & Conditioning Coach") because that is literally what the page source contains; if your fetcher decodes entities, match "Assistant Strength & Conditioning Coach" instead. One quote ("Adrian Mayes - Graduate Assistant - Offense") contains a genuine double space, reproduced verbatim. Wikipedia's dashes are en-dashes (–) except for the Scott Ray and Anthony Schlegel lines, which use hyphens with irregular spacing; all reproduced exactly. WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT. - Scott Ray is included but FLAGGED AS UNCONFIRMED. He appears only in Wikipedia's unsourced staff list and is absent from Ohio State's own October 2014 athletics staff directory, the October 2014 football staff page, and the 2014 media guide. I did not drop him (he is genuinely sourced) but he should not be awarded a ring without independent confirmation. - ANALYSTS / QUALITY CONTROL: I found none, and I believe none existed under that title. Ohio State's 2014 football department table lists four graduate assistants (GAA) and one "Intern" (Derek Chang) and no analyst or QC positions. The `analyst` and `qc` categories are therefore empty - this is a real absence, not a gap in my search. - EQUIPMENT: Ohio State's directory lists equipment staff (Rob Lachey, "Mgr, Athletic Equipment"; Brad Swartz, "Supv, Athletics Equipment") only department-wide, with NO sport assignment. I could not establish that any named equipment person was assigned to football, so I added no `equipment` rows rather than guess. - MEDICAL beyond Doug Calland: the directory lists athletic trainers by FACILITY, not by sport. Six are based at WHAC (the football building): Doug Calland, Bob Sweeney, Jason Rule, Erin Scheper, Michael Sypniak and Shaun Barnhouse. Only Calland is independently confirmed as football's trainer (the media guide's football quick-facts box names him "Head trainer"). The other five are plausible football trainers but the source does not say so, so I excluded them rather than pad. If you want them, they are cited and recoverable from the same directory URL. - ACADEMICS/NUTRITION/SPORTS PSYCHOLOGY: the SASSO academic counselors and sports-psychology staff are listed department-wide with no sport assignment, so no football-specific names could be established. - The February 2015 capture of the staff page (20150208034620) is already the 2015 staff (Tim Beck had replaced Tom Herman), so I used the October 2014 in-season captures as the authoritative snapshot. There is no Wayback capture of these pages between November 2014 and the January 12, 2015 title game; I am relying on October 2014 captures plus the absence of any documented mid-season departure. - I detected and correctly EXCLUDED three names (Patrick Flemming, Bryant Haines, Drew Mehringer) that appear in the raw HTML of the October 2014 staff page but are inside HTML comment blocks - stale 2012-13 graduate assistants left commented out in the template. A naive scrape of that page would wrongly include them. - Web search quota for this session was exhausted before I began, so I could not run contemporary news searches for hire announcements. All findings come from direct URL fetches, Wayback CDX enumeration, and the media guide PDF.
